utterances.text: Both for me and the members of my family. My family members received insurance via the VP 3001 military post. The difference was that for my family members I had to certify the IDs every year, once again in Belgrade, and the military post was 3001 once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The next document I'm going to ask you to look at can be found by turning to the first green tab in tab 5 of Prosecution 505, and it's ERN ending 2886. And that is being displayed on the screen in front of you. Can you summarise what this document is for us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: This is a document on the basis of which my years of service are acknowledged and certified for my pension calculations. It is a document which was issued by the military post 3001, and it says "Confidential," and the date was the 24th of March, 1995. That means that it was through the military post VP 3001, the 30th Personnel Centre, in fact, that we received our pension insurance. We were insured for pensional purposes. Now, what is interesting in this document is point 2, item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I can just ask you to go through each point and ask you a specific question. Point 2 - and it should be visible on the television screen - can I first ask you to read that one sentence, and then I will ask you to comment on its significance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Point 2: This is double the pensionable years during the war, recognised by VP 3001, the 30th Personnel Centre. And for 12 months -- if you'd served 12 months, you would be given 24 months. 24 months would be calculated. And this is something that one benefits when the situations are extremely difficult and when members of the army are in a state of war. Then your years would be double, doubled, your years of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: First I want to read you a particular line. It says here, "Pursuant to Article 156, paragraph 1, and Article 157 of the law on the Yugoslav army --" and it gives several gazette references, one being from 1993 and two being from 1994. Was it your understanding that your pension benefits were determined by VJ law as it was established in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Our pension insurance was determined by the law governing the Army of Yugoslavia and no other laws, because we were members of the 30th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, looking down where the calculation of the credits that you have for your service, there's an entry -- the second entry says that between the 6th of April, 1992 and the 10th of November, 1993 -- and it has some other numbers. But then it has "12/24." What is the significance of 12/24?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: That 12/24 indicates that the person in question -- that the pension credit of 24 months is given for 12 months, and it is the wartime period of service, which is when the members are operational and perform their duties in times of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does the time period 6th of April, 1992 to the 10th of November, 1993 indicate that according to the 30th Personnel Centre that time period was -- was to be considered a combat period for the purposes of calculating your pension?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. According to this document, from the 6th of April, 1992, that is what is being recognised.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before I ask you to look at the second page, on the top right-hand corner of the first page is the title "Years of Service Form." Is that the name that refers to this particular document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes. This is a form. And in the military computer centre, that is where they calculate pension entitlements and the years of service involved are longer than those that were actually involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now if I can ask you to look at the second page of the document -- or I apologise. Perhaps it's all on the same page. I want to draw your attention to the person who signed this document. Can you tell us the name of that person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: The officer in charge who signed this document is Ljubomir Lalic, Colonel, who worked at the 30th Personnel Centre. This was established on the 24th of May, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the seal that we see to the left of his signature, 3001, is that the stamp of the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That is the seal of the 30th Personnel Centre, Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The translation of this document records his last name as being spelled L-a-t-i-c. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Ljubomir Lalic, L-a-l-i-c is correct, so the letter is "L" as in Luxembourg.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was your understanding -- if you had a disagreement about how your pension benefits were calculated, where did you have to go, according to your understanding, to appeal the decision reflected in Lalic's determination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: If anybody would have anything to appeal in this regard, in respect of this decision, it was exactly prescribed, how the appeal were to be carried out, that the appeal should be submitted in two copies to the supreme military court in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now if I can draw your attention to another document, another Year of Service Form. This would be the second green tab or second green sticker in tab 5 of 505, ending in ERN 2884. Can I ask you to just describe this document very briefly for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes. The document is quite identical to the previous one that we had discussed. However, this document was registered by the military post in Banja Luka, and there is a certain delay involved of five or six months in 1995. This is due to the fact that all documents that were written earlier on were written five or six months later in Republika Srpska in this form of document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who was the signatory on this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: This document was signed by the commander of the 851st Battalion, Colonel Bosko Kulic. The 851st Battalion was stationed in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where does this document -- where is it purported that this document was generated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: This document, GS-7, was created in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I can now draw your attention to the next document. This would be the red sticker in tab 5 of Prosecution Exhibit 505, ERN ending 2888. And, sir, could I ask you to briefly describe what type of document we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: This is a document that was issued by the general staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, the Secretary for Mobilisation and Manpower. And it has to do with recognising double number of years of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is this a decision granting you that double years of service benefit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. This decision grants double years of service from the 6th of April, 1992 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is it also signed by Colonel Lalic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes, it was signed by Colonel Ljubomir Lalic, by the authority given him by the chief, and it was signed in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: According to this document, where are you stationed? Where are you posted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: According to this document, I am stationed at military post 3001, Belgrade. For your information, I was never in the war -- never in Belgrade during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from any required training, were you ever posted to any assignment in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And does this document, like the last one, refer to determinations to be made on the basis of law of the Yugoslav army as well as appeals to be made to the Yugoslav army military court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes. This document, if it was adopted on the basis of the law on the Army of Yugoslavia and if I were to have anything to appeal in respect of this document, then I would have to submit that appeal to the supreme military court in Belgrade within 30 days after having received the document myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My last question regarding this document is to ask you to explain the number at the very top of the document. I'd ask you not to read it, but does this -- is this number a personal identification number for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: This is a personnel identification number. It includes the former and the latter parts contained therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The three --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, excuse me. Let us go back to the place of the station, of his station. You referred to from military post 3001 and this document refers to his place of station.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the form reads his name --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- from military post 3001, Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that is your -- his assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: According to this document, he's recorded as serving from that military post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did he not say that he belonged to this unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It is his testimony that he did in fact belong to this unit, although he never served in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: As I understand it, this was the term which was used for officers who were in fact in BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But remained paid and the rest of it, according to the Prosecution, by the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: They were given this military post number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That personal identification number, as it's important for other documents we will look at here, the first three letters are made up of your initials plus the initial of your father; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the first six digits of that seven-digit number is your date of birth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And one final question about this document - and if I could draw the Chamber's attention to the original on the screen - was this document typed up especially for you or was it a form in which just your information was typed into?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: This document was for me only. And inter alia what can be seen in the left-hand corner is that it was submitted to me, that I received a copy, and that it is used for receiving pension benefits -- or rather, my pension entitlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now if I could ask you to look at the last document. This would be marked by a stick -- a blue sticker. And it's 505, tab 5, ERN ending in 2883. I want to ask you some particular questions about this document. First: Do you recognise it and does it pertain to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this document, and it pertains to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And this document, was this document sent to both the 30th Personnel Centre in Belgrade and the specific location in Bosnia where you were actually physically located during this time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: This document was signed and validated in Banja Luka because it says, "The military battalion that is located in Banja Luka." And it says in this document that I am assigned to the 30th Personnel Centre of the general staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where does it say your duty post is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: It does not say here that I was assigned. This has to do with promotion with a particular -- it has to do with a particular date. And then it is said that I am at the 30th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, could I ask you to describe how you were paid during your years of service when you were located in Bosnia. And let's focus on the period after the official withdrawal of the JNA from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: After the withdrawal of the Yugoslav People's Army, or rather, after the establishment of Republika Srpska, the Army of Republika Srpska was established too. And then persons who had served in the JNA until then became -- became persons who were on the payroll of the Army of Yugoslavia, the VJ. And all these persons who were attached to the 30th Personnel Centre were paid by the Army of Yugoslavia, therefore.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During your entire service in the army in Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you ever receive any money in the form of payment from either the VRS army or the Republika Srpska government?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: As for direct payment by the government of Republika Srpska, I did not receive a single dinar from them. Payment was made exclusively in Yugoslav dinars, and it was regulated as follows: We received money in cash. Until the Posavina Corridor was established, this was regulated in the following way: A helicopter went to Belgrade with officers from the financial service, and after the Posavina Corridor was taken, then they travelled by land. As proof of what I got for a given month, there is this form, like the one you see on the screen right now, which shows that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What's depicted on the screen now is Prosecution Exhibit 505, tab 6. The form is a largely illegible form, but do you recognise this as being one of your payslips which you provided to the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes. This is my payslip where my name and surname are referred to, my rank, how much was paid, the first part of my salary, and how much the remainder was. There is a date and also my years of pensionable service. And this was calculated by the military computer centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On your payslip, is it indicated where you were physically posted during your time in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: The military post from Banja Luka is referred to here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is it also indicated on this payment slip where this payment slip originated from, where it was printed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: It is only mentioned here that it was done at the computer centre. I can't really read all of this. It's quite illegible. I received this form from the officers of the financial service as proof of payment, proof of how much money I had received and how much money was paid into my personal account.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've just been handed a hard copy of the document. Is it any more legible on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: It is correct. My name and surname are there and my rank, the date when the payment was made, the military post code, number such and such, Banja Luka, the code of the person concerned, my personal account number, bank account number, and also that this was done by the military computer centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know where that centre was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: I got this from the officers of the financial service when they returned from Belgrade and when they collected our salaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention or turn your attention to the topic of identification papers. While you were serving in Bosnia after the official withdrawal of the JNA, what in the way of identification documents were you issued or did you have in your possession?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: While serving in the Yugoslav People's Army, every officer of the Yugoslav People's Army had to have a military identity card.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you have such a card?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: We did, all the time. For example, when the Yugoslav People's Army withdrew in 1992, and then all the way up to 1996, the main identification document was the ID card of the former Yugoslav People's Army that was validated in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 505, tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is this a photocopy of your identification documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes. This is a copy of my military ID with my name and surname and all the necessary details. Finally, it was validated by military post 3001, Belgrade, and it was valid until 1999, the 31st of December, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I draw your attention to an endorsement of the 31st of December, 1999, an endorsement by Colonel Bosko Mijic. Do you know who he was and where he was assigned?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's ERN number ending 2896.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to make a correction. It's not the way you put it. It was signed by Colonel Gojko Mijic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who was this person? Where was he assigned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: It's a colonel who worked in the 30th Personnel Centre. He worked on these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you just a moment ago referred to endorsements by the 30th Personnel Centre or military post VP 3001. Could I ask you to turn to that page. And that's ERN number ending 2899. Am I correct in saying that of the four endorsements here, three were done in Banja Luka and one was done in Belgrade at the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. One was done in Belgrade, where it says "Military post 3001, Belgrade." And the other one is from the military post in Banja Luka. The first one was when I just started working.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, during the period of your service in Bosnia from 1992 after the JNA officially withdrew up until after 1995, into 1996, were you ever issued a similar document or an official military identification card from the VRS army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Until 1995? Is that what you are asking?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, during that time period, 1992 until 1995, the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: In the period from 1992 to 1996, the only document was this former military ID of the former Yugoslav People's Army that was validated in Belgrade, and that was the only identification document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were in fact issued a military identification card by the Army of the Republika Srpska? And if so, when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: In 1996, when IFOR entered the area, sometime around then, we got IDs of the Army of Republika Srpska that were issued sometime in the month of July or August.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The witness is indicating that he cannot hear. I'd ask maybe the usher to check. Are you able to hear my voice now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: It's this military ID that is on the monitor now. It includes my name and surname and also my identification number, personal identification number, the stamp of the military post that I had been assigned to in the Army of Republika Srpska, where this military post is, and also the date when it was issued. It was issued in August 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The number that's indicated here, is that the same number unique to you that we saw earlier on some of your other personnel documents, consisting of three letters and six digits?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And excuse me, for the record, we are referring to Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Groome, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: For the record, we are referring to Prosecution Exhibit 505, tab 8.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It is the same identification number, because the registration number is identical to the one that was referred to earlier on, with the initials of the name and surname and the first letter of the father's name, and it also includes the date of birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who is the issuing officer of this identification document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: It was issued -- it was issued in Banja Luka, Lieutenant Colonel Kosta Kiso.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you know of that person and where that person was assigned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: That's a lieutenant colonel who was assigned to the ViPVO of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, after August of 1996, you had in your possession two military identification documents, one for the Yugoslav army and one for the Army of Republika Srpska. What was your understanding about which document you were to produce if you were called upon to do so by members of the IFOR force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Well, if IFOR members or, later, SFOR members were to ask for my ID, the only document I would have to show was the one that you just showed on the screen now. Otherwise, if I had shown the previous military Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. ID, there would be the possibility of them arresting me as a member of the Army of Yugoslavia in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the identity number, is that the one used only in the military or is it the one which is -- which can be used as a citizen generally? Because it says, "Citizen's personal identity number."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may ask a few questions to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On this document, are there actually two identification numbers, both military and citizen identification numbers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: First we are going to say that it was issued by military post 7070, Banja Luka. And the first number is the personal identification number of citizens, that is the number that any citizen has, irrespective of the military. And the other one is the registration number of my military ID, issued by the Army of Republika Srpska, which is identical to the previous one. And we've already explained this a short while ago, what these three letters meant, and also the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So six digits. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. To put it very precisely, this is the date of birth, the first two digits, the day, and the second -- the third and fourth are the month of birth, and the following two are the year of birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This system that you've described with respect to your military identification documents, was this something that was unique to you or are you aware of other officers in similar situations with similar sets of documents issued in the way you've described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-127
utterances.text: Documents of this kind, like the ones I showed, were ones that all the members of the 30th Personnel Centre had.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, is that a convenient place to break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn now. Witness B-127, we must ask you to come back, please, next Tuesday. I'm sorry we won't be sitting for the next few days. If you would come back on Tuesday, we'll conclude your evidence then. How much longer do you think you might be, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think about 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
